summary.prose: Migrate obsolete review tests in five focused tasks while preserving transport, worker/token, persistence, isolation and retained-history/lifecycle controls. Run current baselines and map each valid old assertion to a surviving control; no production review implementation or compatibility shim is added.

tasks.title: Migrate review boundary and client assertions
tasks.summary: Capture focused baseline and assertion map; align review-specific labels, lifecycle wiring, in-daemon client and MCP checks with exact unavailable responses. Move valid generic transport assertions to supported or explicit test-only handlers.
acceptanceChecks: Retired design/code surfaces reject with exact current family response before poisoned-argument reads, providers or IO; no synthetic success on review-named surfaces.
Progress/done, synchronous throws, cancellation/drain and cwd/repo lookup retain equivalent positive controls on supported/test-only generic methods.
Review-only label expectations change without weakening active model-role tier assertions or modifying production review/RPC classification.
Record baseline and old-assertion→current-control mapping; preserve meaningful assertions rather than skipping/deleting suites.

tests.name: Retired review surfaces reject before argument inspection, providers or IO
Generic client progress, synchronous errors and abort drains retain coverage on supported handlers
Review-only label assertions reflect unavailable execution without changing active role tier tests

tasks.title: Migrate worker routing and token lifecycle fixtures
tasks.summary: Update indexing-port, router-session and s3 acceptance review assumptions to current supported operations/kinds while preserving worker ownership and session lifecycle coverage.
acceptanceChecks: Current analyze/workflow token mint/read/update behavior survives idle worker release, with session isolation and old-token semantics preserved.
Retired review/code-review kinds reject without fabricated tokens; no worker/provider review execution restored.
Supported routing/indexing-port controls retain worker identity and shared/session placement evidence using real workers where the original test requires them.
Use bounded readiness, owned worker cleanup and fresh focused baseline; classify unrelated RPC/mutable-state failures separately without editing production method tables.

tests.name: Supported worker tokens survive idle release and preserve session isolation while retired kinds reject

tasks.title: Repair current persistence fixture entry points
tasks.summary: Remove the deleted provenance writer import and map its valid assertions to current guarded boundaries/sinks and saved artifact/history controls, preserving the complete canary matrix.
acceptanceChecks: Persistence fixture imports current modules and executes real assertions rather than failing during module loading.
Temporary task/report/checkpoint/history/trace/cache/vector canaries remain absent from durable sinks; hostile getters remain unread at boundaries that guarantee preflight rejection.
Saved artifact/history/cache/trace positive controls demonstrably persist and read back; no fake review records or resurrected writer export.
Document replacement assertion mapping; if current APIs expose an independent production defect, triage it separately and do not weaken the test or claim green.

tests.name: Temporary persistence canaries remain absent while saved artifact and history controls persist

tasks.title: Replace deleted review isolation inventory entries
tasks.summary: Update store-isolation inventories to exercise current real coverage after the repaired fixtures are available. Preserve default-path negative evidence and deliberate-opening positive controls for graph and vectors.
acceptanceChecks: Each removed fixture entry has a mapped current test/control, with real child execution proven by exit status and TAP cases; empty, skipped-only or failed child runs cannot prove isolation.
Isolated HOME is established before application imports, and no live default LMDB/Lance artifact is created by the applicable current fixtures.
Deliberate default-store-opening positive controls remain and prove the audit can detect violations.
Only review-related inventory drift changes; unrelated failing fixture contracts remain visible in evidence rather than being removed or reclassified to force a pass.
Replacement suites contain named applicable assertions with positive TAP counts and verified normal cleanup; forced exit alone never proves closure or isolation.

tests.name: Current isolation inventories execute real tests and detect deliberate default-store opening

tasks.title: Validate preserved history and publish Batch 04 evidence
tasks.summary: Run final focused groups sequentially, verify retained history and human lifecycle/integrity guarantees, and record actual outcomes, assertion mappings, cleanup and remaining sibling failures.
acceptanceChecks: All seven LLD test subjects and ac1–ac4 map to actual test evidence; current retained history/rendering, human approval, integrity and task/build completion controls pass without fake review entries.
Root typecheck and appropriate source/compiled checks run under supported Node22 with exact pass/fail/skip/cancel counts and confirmed actor closure; no overlapping broad sweeps.
Audit and batch index preserve original observations, replacement mappings and remaining defects; do not claim green for failed/incomplete cases or refresh qualification evidence.
Document unchanged production behavior/API/data and visual relevance; no new review implementation, RPC classification, deprecated IDE compatibility or untracked production fix.
Any independent defect that prevents an acceptance check leaves that task non-green until resolved through an approved tracked path; final evidence distinguishes completed and blocked work.

tests.name: Retained review history and human lifecycle gates remain readable and enforced
Batch 04 assertion mapping, actual focused results and actor closure are recorded
